paragraphs.title: God's Governance of the Wicked and the Suffering

answers: Suffer him a little and listen
easy.explanation: Elihu asks Job to suffer him a little while he continues to speak on God's behalf.
easy.q: What does Elihu ask Job to do at the beginning of his speech?

easy.explanation: The KJV says that God gives “right to the poor.”
easy.q: What does God give to the poor?

answers: They perish by the sword and die without knowledge
easy.explanation: Those who do not obey perish by the sword and die without knowledge.
easy.q: What happens to those who do not obey?

answers: So they may return from iniquity
So they may boast of their strength
So they may ask for riches
medium.explanation: God shows them their work and transgressions and commands them to return from iniquity.
medium.q: Why does God show people their transgressions?

medium.explanation: “Fetters” are chains or restraints, representing affliction and captivity.
medium.q: What does “fetters” mean in this passage?

answers: The obedient spend their days in prosperity, while the disobedient perish
The obedient become kings, while the disobedient become rich
The obedient are punished, while the disobedient are delivered
medium.explanation: Those who obey and serve spend their days in prosperity; those who refuse perish by the sword.
medium.q: What is the difference between those who obey and serve God and those who do not?

answers: Affliction can be used to instruct a person and lead him to repentance
Every person in chains is innocent
God makes no distinction between the righteous and the wicked
challenge.explanation: Affliction is presented as a setting in which God reveals sin and calls people back from iniquity.
challenge.q: What principle about suffering emerges from the connection between affliction and the revealing of transgressions?

answers: God watches over and preserves the righteous
challenge.explanation: God's eyes remain upon the righteous, showing His continued care and attention.
challenge.q: What does the statement that God does not withdraw His eyes from the righteous teach?

answers: People may obey and serve or refuse and perish
Only kings can choose their path
challenge.explanation: The passage sets before people two paths: obedience leading to prosperity, or refusal leading to destruction.
challenge.q: How is human choice presented in this passage?

paragraphs.title: Job's Suffering and the Warning Against Sin

easy.explanation: Elihu says God would have removed Job from the strait into a broad place.
easy.q: What could Job's affliction have removed him from?

easy.explanation: Elihu says, “Take heed, regard not iniquity.”
easy.q: What does Elihu warn Job not to regard?

easy.explanation: Elihu says that a great ransom cannot deliver Job from God's stroke.
easy.q: What cannot deliver Job according to Elihu?

answers: Affliction may lead him from a strait place into a broad place
Affliction proves that he has no hope
Affliction is meant to separate him from everyone
medium.explanation: Elihu describes God as able to remove Job from a place of distress into a broad and comfortable place.
medium.q: What connection does Elihu make between Job's affliction and his possible deliverance?

medium.explanation: In context, “fulfilled” means completed or filled up the judgment.
medium.q: What does “fulfilled” mean in “thou hast fulfilled the judgment of the wicked”?

answers: He warns Job against seeking escape through sinful or rebellious means
The night is only meant for sleeping
It is forbidden to speak about nations
medium.explanation: The warning fits Elihu's call to reject iniquity rather than seek relief through rebellion or wrongdoing.
medium.q: Why does Elihu tell Job not to desire the night when people are cut off?

answers: It can awaken a person to seek God and escape danger
It prevents a person from understanding anything
challenge.explanation: Affliction may move a person toward deliverance, repentance, and a cry for help.
challenge.q: What role does Elihu give to affliction?

answers: Accepting God's judgment keeps Job from turning to wrong paths in despair
Accepting judgment means Job must stop thinking
challenge.explanation: Elihu warns Job not to let trouble or anger lead him toward iniquity.
challenge.q: How are accepting judgment and avoiding sin connected in Elihu's warning?

answers: Riches cannot secure God's favor or deliver a person from judgment
challenge.explanation: Elihu says that neither riches, gold, nor strength can provide ultimate deliverance.
challenge.q: What does the question “Will he esteem thy riches?” emphasize?

paragraphs.title: God's Greatness and the Impossibility of Challenging Him

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “God exalteth by his power.”
easy.q: By what does God exalt Himself?

easy.explanation: Elihu asks, “Who teacheth like him?” showing that no one can instruct God.
easy.q: Who can teach God His way?

easy.explanation: The passage says that the number of God's years cannot be searched out.
easy.q: What cannot be searched out completely?

answers: That a person has the right to accuse God of wrongdoing
That God works in the world
That people can see God's works
medium.explanation: Elihu emphasizes that no human being can rightly accuse God of iniquity.
medium.q: What claim does Elihu reject by asking who can say to God, “Thou hast wrought iniquity”?

answers: Exalted or far beyond human measure
medium.explanation: Here “great” describes God's surpassing greatness and majesty.
medium.q: What does “great” mean in the statement, “God is great”?

answers: They can behold and magnify them, but cannot fully search out God
They can command them, but cannot see them
They can neither see nor praise them
medium.explanation: People may behold and magnify God's works, yet God's greatness and years remain beyond full human understanding.
medium.q: What can people do concerning God's works, and what can they not do?

answers: Human beings are limited in their ability to judge and understand God
challenge.explanation: The questions emphasize God's authority and the limits of human judgment.
challenge.q: What message emerges from the questions about who can teach God and who can accuse Him?

answers: People can see His works, but His greatness remains beyond full searching
There are no divine works in the world
People are forbidden to look at the heavens
challenge.explanation: The passage allows people to behold God's works while insisting that God Himself cannot be fully comprehended.
challenge.q: Why does observing God's works not result in complete knowledge of God?

answers: Humility and recognition of God's superiority
challenge.explanation: God's power, wisdom, and incomprehensible greatness call for humility rather than challenge.
challenge.q: What attitude does Elihu require from Job toward God?

paragraphs.title: Rain, Clouds, and Thunder as Expressions of God's Work

easy.explanation: The passage describes drops of water pouring down as rain.
easy.q: What comes down from the clouds?

easy.explanation: The clouds drop and distil rain upon people abundantly.
easy.q: What do the clouds drop and distil?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “he giveth meat in abundance.”
easy.q: What does God give in abundance through these forces?

answers: Water, clouds, rain, light, and thunder
medium.explanation: Elihu describes water drops, clouds, rain, light, and the noise of the storm.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes Elihu's picture?

answers: The clouds extending or spreading across the sky
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the broad expanse and movement of clouds.
medium.q: What are “the spreadings of the clouds”?

answers: God uses them both to judge people and to give food abundantly
medium.explanation: The passage says that through these forces God judges the people and gives them food.
medium.q: How do these natural forces affect people?

answers: To show that God's works are complex and beyond human understanding
To prove that rain has no importance
To describe a journey made by people
challenge.explanation: The many details of the storm show the greatness and mystery of God's activity.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of Elihu's description of the water cycle and the heavens?

answers: The same divine power can bring both judgment and provision
God gives food only to kings
challenge.explanation: Elihu presents the forces of heaven as instruments through which God both judges and provides.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the connection between God judging the people and giving meat in abundance?

answers: Light spreading across the cloud or sky
challenge.explanation: The verse pictures God's light spread across the storm clouds and heavens.
challenge.q: What does “he spreadeth his light upon it” describe?
